Timot. 2.", then a paragraph opened by a large woodcut initial, running to the foot of the page. No marginal notes, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.l: que noftri fpiritus & animæ, & corpora cri-
Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui nos de manu
inimicorum nostrorum liberavit, ut sine ti-
more serviremus ipsi cum sanctitate & justi-
tia coram ipso, cunctis diebus vitæ nostræ:
cui sit honor in secula, Amen.

l.i: O[?]olo igitur orare viros in omni loco
sustollentes puras manus, absque ira & disce-
mulieres in amictu modesto, cum vere-
tortis crinibus, aut auro, aut margaritis,
aut vestitu sumptuoso, sed quod decet
opera. Mulier in silentio discat cum omni
usurpare in viros, sed esse in silentio. Adam
enim prior formatus est, deinde Eva. Et
Adam non fuit deceptus, sed mulier
sioni: salva tamen fiet per generationem

page.notes: The woodcut initial at the start of the italic paragraph is decorative; the first word is read as "Olo" with a doubtful first letter, most likely V (Volo, 1 Tim. 2:8), marked [?]. "Consimiliter" is read with some doubt in the word-start letters. Small pen-like marks in the right margin and along the lines are not printed text and are left out. The page ends mid-sentence ("per generationem"), so the paragraph continues on the next page.
